from django.db import connection
from django.test import TestCase, skipUnlessDBFeature
from queries.models import ReservedName

@skipUnlessDBFeature('supports_select_union')
class UnionMutateTest(TestCase):
    def test_values_list_on_combined_qs(self):
        """Test values()/values_list() on combined qs doesn't mutate select cols."""
        ReservedName.objects.create(name='a', order=1)
        ReservedName.objects.create(name='b', order=2)

        qs1 = ReservedName.objects.all()
        reserved_name = qs1.union(qs1).values_list('name', 'order', 'id').get()
        self.assertEqual(reserved_name[:2], ('a', 2))
        # Now check qs1 hasn't been mutated
        print("qs1 values_select:", qs1.query.values_select)
        print("qs1 default_cols:", qs1.query.default_cols)
        print("qs1 select:", qs1.query.select)
        print("qs1.union(qs1).query.values_select:", qs1.union(qs1).query.values_select)
        
    def test_union_values_list_no_mutation(self):
        qs1 = ReservedName.objects.all()
        # Call values_list on the union result  
        union_values = qs1.union(qs1).values_list('order')
        result = list(union_values)
        print("union values_list result:", result)
        # Now evaluate qs1 directly - should not be affected
        print("qs1 values_select:", qs1.query.values_select)
        print("qs1 default_cols:", qs1.query.default_cols)
        print("qs1 select:", qs1.query.select)
        result2 = list(qs1)
        print("qs1 objects:", result2)
        # Call values on qs1 - should give full results
        result3 = list(qs1.values())
        print("qs1.values():", result3)

    def test_union_with_ordering_field_not_in_select(self):
        """The bug scenario: qs has ordering, derived qs changes select list."""
        ReservedName.objects.create(name='a', order=1)
        ReservedName.objects.create(name='b', order=2)
        ReservedName.objects.create(name='c', order=3)

        qs = ReservedName.objects.all().order_by('order')
        # Evaluate qs - this compiles and executes SQL, but doesn't cache
        # (simulating interactive display which uses slicing)
        print("qs[:10]:", list(qs[:10]))
        
        # Now derive and evaluate
        derived = qs.order_by().values_list('pk', flat=True)
        print("derived:", list(derived))
        
        # Re-evaluate original
        print("qs[:10] again:", list(qs[:10]))
        
EOF

import copy
from django.test import TestCase
from queries.models import ReservedName

ATTRS = ['values_select', 'default_cols', 'select', 'order_by', 'default_ordering',
         'standard_ordering', 'extra_order_by', 'high_mark', 'low_mark', 'combinator',
         'annotation_select_mask', 'extra_select_mask', 'subquery', 'group_by', 'distinct']

def snap(q):
    d = {a: getattr(q, a, '<missing>') for a in ATTRS}
    d['alias_refcount'] = dict(q.alias_refcount)
    d['alias_map'] = sorted(q.alias_map)
    d['annotations'] = sorted(q.annotations)
    d['used_aliases'] = set(q.used_aliases)
    d['table_map'] = {k: list(v) for k, v in q.table_map.items()}
    return d

class T(TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpTestData(cls):
        for i in range(1, 5):
            ReservedName.objects.create(name='n%d' % i, order=i)

    def test_mutation_detect(self):
        A = ReservedName.objects.filter(pk__in=[1, 2])
        B = ReservedName.objects.filter(pk__in=[3, 4])
        qs = A.union(B).order_by('order')
        sa, sb = snap(A.query), snap(B.query)
        list(qs)
        for label, derived in [
            ('order_by().values_list', qs.order_by().values_list('pk', flat=True)),
            ('values_list', qs.values_list('pk', flat=True)),
            ('count', None),
            ('slice', qs[:2]),
            ('order_by(name)', qs.order_by('name')),
        ]:
            if derived is None:
                qs.count()
            else:
                list(derived)
            na, nb = snap(A.query), snap(B.query)
            for k in na:
                if na[k] != sa[k]:
                    print('MUTATION A after', label, ':', k, sa[k], '->', na[k])
                if nb[k] != sb[k]:
                    print('MUTATION B after', label, ':', k, sb[k], '->', nb[k])
            sa, sb = na, nb
        print('final qs sql:', qs.query)
        print('final qs:', list(qs))
